NeykovBalakrishnanWasserman2021 supplies conditional-independence lower-bound machinery but not null priors whose every draw has constant CATE.
CrumpHotzImbensMitnik2008, ChangLeeWhang2015, DaiShenStern2023, and DaiStern2022 give direct asymptotic heterogeneity tests, not the proposed fixed-sample three-index minimax frontier.
Hahn1998 concerns regular ATE efficiency; no inspected source gives a necessary-and-sufficient known-versus-unknown propensity testing-radius frontier.

novelty_flags.label: Open-ended Question 2 / related_work
novelty_flags.one_line: The direct predecessor survey omits DaiStern2022, a published U-statistic nonparametric test of equality of treatment effects across subgroups, and SantAnna2021, a published nonparametric HTE-testing extension; distinguish both from the continuous-Hölder minimax target.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper derives minimax rates for Hölder-smooth pointwise CATE estimation and explicitly identifies global L2 rates and CATE testing as future directions rather than proving a homogeneity-testing critical radius.

source_verification_receipts.version: Review of Economics and Statistics 90(3), 2008, pp. 389–405
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper develops series/sieve nonparametric tests, including the null that the conditional average effect is constant across covariate-defined subpopulations; it is a direct asymptotic predecessor rather than a fixed-sample Hölder minimax-radius result.

The article uses L1 functionals of kernel conditional-mean estimators, establishes asymptotically correct size and fixed/local-alternative power, and includes zero conditional average-effect restrictions.
The article proposes a propensity-reweighted multisample U-statistic test for observational treatment-effect heterogeneity and establishes asymptotic normality.

The paper proposes a U-statistic-based nonparametric test of equality of treatment effects across subgroups; it is a missing direct published comparator, though it does not state the proposed continuous-Hölder minimax problem.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:2410.00985v4; JASA accepted-author version posted 18 May 2026
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies quantitative and qualitative CATE-homogeneity tests with asymptotic inferential guarantees; no final paginated JASA version was available for theorem-number verification.
The preprint tests the variance-zero CATE-homogeneity null using intra-fold splitting and claims consistency, asymptotic normality, and type-I control under learner-rate conditions.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add DaiStern2022 and SantAnna2021 to related_work, state their nulls, sampling geometry, and asymptotic guarantees, and explain why neither yields a continuous-covariate three-index Hölder radius.

Add a worked finite instance evaluating both r_test and r_mix, including the active resolution and divergence constraint, so the two proposed deterministic objects are auditable before the full matching proof.

After the survey repair, make the comparison frontier sharper by stating the exact strict-inclusion relation between the proposed uniform full-support class and the support-restricted lower constructions used by KBRW.
